title: A finite ring map is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $T$, viewed as an $R$-module via $\varphi$, is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $R\to T$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $R\to T$ is quasi-finite at every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PM (lemma-quasi-finite, line 30265), direction 'fibres finite implies quasi-finite', via Lemma Tag 0H8X (lemma-quasi-finite-above-p, line 30245, (2) implies (1)); applied to a finite ring map, whose fibre rings $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras; as used in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open, line 30891). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags.

proof.text: Choose $t_1,\dots,t_n\in T$ generating $T$ as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The $R$-subalgebra generated by these elements contains every $R$-linear combination of them, hence is all of $T$. Equivalently the evaluation map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to T$, $x_i\mapsto t_i$, is surjective, so $R\to T$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The empty list covers the zero ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PM (lemma-quasi-finite, line 30265), finite-type hypothesis; finite module generators also generate the algebra

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=T\otimes_Rk$, the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Every element of $F$ is a sum of pure tensors $t\otimes\lambda$. Writing $t=\sum_i r_it_i$ by step 1 gives $t\otimes\lambda=\sum_i(t_i\otimes1)(\varphi_k(r_i)\lambda)$, where $\varphi_k:R\to k$ is the canonical map. Thus the finitely many $t_i\otimes1$ span $F$ as a $k$-vector space; $k\to F$ is a finite ring map.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0H8X (lemma-quasi-finite-above-p, line 30245), condition (2), applied to a finite algebra; the finite base change is the displayed spanning calculation

proof.text: The field $k$ is a local ring whose only prime is $(0)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] to the finite $k$-algebra $F$ of step 2: $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a finite discrete space, so each of its points is open. This includes the zero-ring fibre, whose spectrum is empty.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0H8X (lemma-quasi-finite-above-p, line 30245), (2) implies (1), using discreteness of the finite fibre; the cited leaf follows Lemma Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian, line 42571)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be any prime, and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] there is a unique corresponding prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $F=T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Step 3 says $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Together with the finite-type conclusion of step 1, this is precisely that $R\to T$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Since $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, the assertion holds at every prime.
